title: rwb-integration rule copy: the H and C rows, the model-fetch surface, the assigned package, the local copy table, the event consumers and the login are not settled by any one source
source: WP B-P2-03; legacy RWB-E1-073 (sections 4, 9, 11, 12, 13 and 16); RWB-ITG-E1073-ITG sections 3, 10, 12 and 16; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 16, 20, 27, 28, 41, 43 row 30 and 44 JOB-20; Recovery Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 11, 12, 14, 15 and 16; FSD P2 Integration v3 A2.1 to A2.7; TSD P2 Integration v3 T2; Plan Appendix R section R3 default ruling; Template and Rules v1 sections R5.5 (DP-01 to DP-19), R5.7 and R9
description: One combined gap covers everything this slice cannot read from a single source. (1) The plan sets Depends on (build) to None while the DP table adds eight H rows for the patterns this story applies, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (DP-03), RWB-PLT-E1072-CON (DP-04), RWB-PLT-E1042-CON (DP-06), RWB-PLT-E1043-CON (DP-07), RWB-PLT-E1071-CON (DP-10), RWB-PLT-E1047-CON (DP-14), RWB-PLT-E1044-CON (DP-15) and RWB-PLT-N001-CON (DP-19). (2) The contract-dependency row carries RWB-P3-E1073-CON while the DP-04 row names C RWB-P7-E1073-CON, and the model fetch is P7's operation. (3) Architecture v5 slide 43 row 30 names rwb-case, rwb-valuation, rwb-treatment and rwb-payment as the consumers of RulePackageInForce while slide 20 says every service refreshes its cache on it; this story reads slide 20, which is what makes rwb-integration an evaluator, and the event payload beyond package code, version label, checksum and valid from is given nowhere. (4) The plan and the design decks name no package code assigned to rwb-integration, so the legacy ALLOCATION fixtures ALLOCATION, ALLOC-2026.11, ALLOC-2026.12, ALLOC-2026.13, TRF-2026.11, the rows ALLOC-014, ALLOC-015, ALLOC-031, ALLOC-032, ALLOC-040, ALLOC-041, ALLOC-999, the scenarios TA-07 and TA-19, the queues MTG-BKK-CO, MTG-UPC-CO, MTG-CEN-CO and GEN-CO, 24 and 26 rows, 50 scenarios, checksum 9f2c...e1b4 and valid from 2026-12-15 are used as synthetic test data only. (5) The model fetch is named GET /rule-models/{n}/{v} on Architecture v5 slides 14 and 27 and appears in neither the Ownership Map nor API Specification v4, so its path segments and its request and response fields are unsettled. (6) The local copy table name and columns are given by no source, and the parameter read path and list code of the rwb-case contracts are equally unstated. (7) The rwb-integration login name (DP-02) is given nowhere; the legacy story ran on the shared recovery_svc login.
evidence: WP B-P2-03 story line for RWB-P2-E1073-APP ("H": [], "C": ["RWB-P3-E1073-CON"], patterns DP01 to DP19). Template and Rules v1 section R5.5: DP-03 adds H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, DP-04 adds H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON, DP-06 adds H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, DP-07 adds H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, DP-10 adds H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, DP-14 adds H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, DP-15 adds H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, DP-19 adds H RWB-PLT-N001-CON. Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 (P2 rwb-integration owns interface config, file runs, outbound items, schema rwb_integration, topic rwb.integration.events.v1, queue rwb-integration, wave 1) and slide 20 (every service from the template: own schema with outbox, inbox and decision_record; RulePackageInForce to cache refresh). Slide 43 row 30 (RulePackageInForce consumers: rwb-case, rwb-valuation, rwb-treatment, rwb-payment). Slides 14 and 27 (GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}, verify checksum, swap in; governance central, evaluation local, last good model kept). Slide 44 JOB-20 (rule promote 00:01, rwb-decision, Schedule to RulePackageInForce). Temporal and Drools design slides 11, 12, 14, 15 and 16 (embedded kit, EvaluateRules and RecordAndApply per service queue, checksum before swap, KieBaseRegistry LRU max 20, first match writes the rule ID). FSD P2 Integration v3 A2.1 to A2.7 step 1 ("Reads the version of the rules in force") and step 3 ("Writes the decision log entry"). TSD P2 Integration v3 T2 (IntegrationService "calls the rules component; writes the decision log entry before any change"). Legacy RWB-E1-073 section 12 (five admin endpoints, no model fetch) and section 16 (twenty test cases, System and Access).
area: Rule package ownership, consumed contract rows and the local rule copy
proposed: Keep the plan's H and C lists as the story is written and record the eight DP H rows as wave-0 platform prerequisites in the Service Contract Catalog; publish the model fetch in RWB-P7-E1073-CON with the path, the request and the response fields agreed at the contract review; keep the ALLOCATION set as synthetic fixture data in the test environment only and replace it with the assigned package when the reference data names it; fix the local copy table, columns and migration in the rwb_integration DB story; name the login before the rwb_integration baseline is created.

title: rwb-integration ALS settlement booking: the interface itself, the modelling of INT-03, the field mapping, the metadata rows and the login are not settled by any one source
source: WP B-P2-03; legacy RWB-E4-046; RWB-ITG-E4046-ITG sections 4, 11, 12 and 19; Ownership Map v1 (interface_config, outbound_item and job_catalog to P2; treatment to S2; document to P5; recovery_case and task to P3; decision_log_entry to P7); FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5 (outbound interface register: INT-14, INT-19, INT-20, INT-25 only) and T5.1 note; TSD P2 Integration v3 T1 (INT-03 core bank bookings are manual, no Workbench interface), T3.1, T4, T5.1, T6.1 and T-A.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 16, 20, 41, 43 and 44; Template and Rules v1 section R7.1, R5.5 DP-02, DP-03 and DP-19
description: One combined gap covers everything this slice cannot read from a single source. (a) The FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5 register and the TSD P2 Integration v3 T1 and T5.1 say INT-03 core-bank bookings have NO Workbench interface: the officer books the restructure, settlement or write-off in the core bank and the booking is confirmed on the next ACE batch through v_ace_account. The legacy story RWB-E4-046 and RWB-ITG-E4046-ITG model the ALS booking as an outbound item on an interface configuration row. This story follows the legacy key and the integration story, and records the conflict instead of repairing it: one row of the register and one line of the TSD are superseded for this legacy key, and the read-back half of the legacy journey stays with rwb-source-data after the next ACE batch. (b) The ALS interface id, its transport, the message or file layout, its result codes and its retry intervals and maximum attempts are given by no source: the FSD register names four interfaces only (INT-14, INT-19, INT-20, INT-25) and the retry values it shows are the example values of the WIN file (attempt 2 five minutes after attempt 1, attempt 3 fifteen minutes after attempt 2, three attempts for INT-14 and INT-25), not the ALS values. This story therefore builds the reader and the lifecycle and leaves every value a row of the interface configuration, cited as the placeholder. (c) The metadata H row of the story is None, as the plan fixes it, while DP-03 adds H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and DP-19 adds H RWB-PLT-N001-CON; both platform contracts are delivered by the platform wave and neither blocks Day 1. (d) The story is given no C row at all, although the journey touches the rwb-treatment contract at its caller and the rwb-document, rwb-case and rwb-access contracts at its consumed edges; the row stays None because the story owns no build wait of another service. (e) The rwb-integration login name of DP-02 is given nowhere; the legacy story ran on the shared recovery_svc identity. (f) Which field ID of outbound_item carries each element of the ALS message or file is not specified: TSD P2 v3 T3.1 publishes the ten fields of the table but not the mapping of the ALS layout to them, and no source gives the task code of the owner task the exception queue raises.
evidence: FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5 (the outbound register holds INT-14, INT-19, INT-20 and INT-25, each an interface_config row with direction OUT) and A2.1.4.3 AC-EXC-P2-001-01 and AC-EXC-P2-001-04 (the retry and exception behaviour, the 5 and 15 minute example intervals, the resend to PENDING with attempt count 0 and MSG-GEN-005); TSD P2 Integration v3 T1 ('INT-03 core bank bookings are manual: the officer books the restructure, settlement or write-off in the core bank, and the booking is confirmed on the next ACE batch through v_ace_account') and T5.1 (INT-03 'Workbench: no interface'), T3.1 (interface_config DF-OPS-136 to DF-OPS-148, outbound_item DF-OPS-168 to DF-OPS-177), T4 ('a failed send or failed outbound check moves to RETRY at the retry_intervals_min of its interface_config version; after max_attempts (three for INT-14 and INT-25) it moves to EXCEPTION and a task goes to owner_role') and T-A.1/T-A.2 (API-P2-001 and API-P2-002); Architecture v5 slides 11 (Idempotency-Key on every POST, claim-check file, FileFailed event and operator retry), 16 and 41 (rwb-integration owns interface config, file runs and outbound items, topic rwb.integration.events.v1 with FileDelivered and FileFailed, 'events (none: called as a task)', queue rwb-integration), 20 (every service: own schema with outbox, inbox and decision_record), 43 (FileDelivered and FileFailed consumed by the requesting service) and 44 (no shared Quartz table; no ALS file window); legacy RWB-E4-046 AC1 and AC2 (outbound_item, v_ace_account and v_ace_payment read-back, MSG-P7-003) and legacy RWB-E1-007 section 14 (MSG-P2-001 and MSG-GEN-005 texts, the task for the owner role, SCR-09); RWB-ITG-E4046-ITG steps 4, 5, 10 and section 19 (the ALS booking as an outbound item, the exception queue, 'The rwb-integration interface build, the outbound item lifecycle, the retry and the exception queue') and its section 3 and 7 (the ALS interface ID, transport, layout and test endpoint are not specified); Ownership Map v1 rows for interface_config, outbound_item, job_catalog, treatment, document, recovery_case, task and decision_log_entry.
area: Outbound interface configuration, item lifecycle and integration boundary
proposed: Keep the reading of RWB-ITG-E4046-ITG and of the legacy key: the ALS settlement booking is one outbound item on an interface configuration row of rwb-integration, and the FSD A1.5 register and the TSD T1 and T5.1 line on INT-03 are marked superseded for this legacy key in the Service Contract Catalog, with the date and the decision. Agree the ALS interface id, transport, layout, result codes, maximum attempts and retry intervals with the interface owner and load them as one versioned interface_config row per environment, citing them instead of naming them in code or in a story. Keep the metadata H row at None and record that DP-03 and DP-19 add the two platform contracts that the platform wave delivers. Name the rwb-integration login before the rwb_integration baseline is created, and agree the task code of the owner task and the field mapping of the ALS layout with the rwb-case owner and the interface owner at the contract review of RWB-P2-E1007-CON.
